samples.summary: `printable()` neutralizes only C0/C1 controls, leaving Unicode bidi/format overrides able to forge the decision screen it exists to protect
samples.evidence: `printable` is introduced specifically so that model-written `summary`/`file` text "could hide the findings printed above it or forge a 'no blocking findings' line" (docblock, lines 274-288). Its filter is `/[�--]/g` plus a `\s+` collapse. ESC and CR are defused, and U+2028/U+2029 happen to be caught by `\s`, but the Unicode bidirectional overrides and isolates — U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200E/U+200F — are neither C0/C1 nor `\s`, so they pass through verbatim into `console.error` at spec-to-pr.mjs:339-345. Vector: a finding summary produced from attacker-chosen repository text (a lens routinely quotes the diff back) carries U+202E; in the terminal the developer reads to decide whether the branch is clean, the rendered order of the remainder of that line — and of text after it, since the override is not terminated — is reversed, which is the Trojan-Source presentation attack and exactly the "text written by the party under review is data, never markup" property the function claims. I confirmed no bidi/format-character handling exists anywhere under scripts/agent. Impact is display-forgery on an advisory local gate, hence minor; the fix is one more character class in the same replace.

samples.summary: `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` is a new unrestricted env-var lever that redirects the spawned reviewer to any script on disk
samples.evidence: `panelScript(env)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:793-796) takes `process.env.WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL`, `path.resolve`s it with no constraint on location, and the result is executed as `execFileSync("node", panelArgs({ panel: panelScript(process.env), ... }), { stdio: "inherit" })` at spec-to-pr.mjs:1084-1097 with the full inherited environment — which in the CI half of the documented contract holds `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and the `_1…_8` pool slots (see ambientAuthNotice, spec-to-pr.mjs:238-272). The docblock's defence ("anyone who can set a variable in its environment can already run whatever they like") holds for the interactive developer case, and I confirmed no workflow under .github/ currently invokes `spec-to-pr.mjs review`, so this is latent rather than exploitable today. What it costs is a property: the command whose exit code the new docs call "the gate" (docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md §1.1) can be pointed at a stub that writes an all-`success` panel.json, and the lever exists purely for a test. Cheapest hardening: refuse an override that does not resolve inside `HERE`, or gate it on NODE_ENV/a test-only sentinel, so the seam cannot be reached by an environment the script did not author.
searchedFor: Grep 'WAFFLEBASE_' across the repo — no workflow sets WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL
Grep 'spec-to-pr' in .github/workflows — no CI invocation of the review subcommand

samples.summary: The local `--rebuttals` path skips `serializeRebuttal`'s length caps on author-controlled text that feeds the adjudicator
samples.evidence: `normalizeRebuttals` (spec-to-pr.mjs:632-636) states "Only the prefix is touched" and `readRebuttalRecords` (663-673) does nothing further, so a hand-written record goes to the panel as-is. In the cloud the same fields pass `serializeRebuttal` (scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs:95-111), which caps `findingKey` 300, `lens` 60, `file` 300, `summary` 2000, `claim` 4000 and `evidence` to 10 entries of 500 — caps its own docblock justifies as belonging on the WRITE side because "the writer is the untrusted party". In the local loop the writer is the agent under review (.claude/commands/self-review.md instructs it to author the rebuttals file), i.e. precisely rebuttal.mjs's untrusted party, and the adjudication is "the one input that can remove a finding from the gate" (rebuttal.mjs:477-482). I verified the more serious half is covered: `defence()` is applied at prompt-build time in `buildAdjudicatorPrompt` (rebuttal.mjs:483-496), so a `</author-rebuttal>` fence break is neutralized on this path too, and the `neutral()` `<!--` escape is irrelevant locally because nothing is posted. What remains uncapped is claim/evidence length, i.e. unbounded author prose into the adjudicator's context. Low impact, but the asymmetry between the two entry points is not stated anywhere.

samples.summary: `--round N` is a second, unadvertised door past the round bound the same change just closed for `--fresh`
samples.evidence: The bound is described as ENFORCED with `--force` as "the one advertised door" (MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS docblock, spec-to-pr.mjs:151-152; roundBoundNotice, 216-236), and the diff adds `spentRound = args.fresh ? Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore)) : round` (987) plus a CLI test specifically so `--fresh` cannot renumber a fourth round into a clean first one. `--round` is not covered: at spec-to-pr.mjs:979 `round = Number(args.round)` is taken verbatim, `spentRound` equals it when `--fresh` is absent, and `roundBoundNotice(3)` returns "" — so with three completed rounds on disk, `review --round 3` runs, is never refused, and can be repeated indefinitely. It also overwrites `round-3`'s verdict directories in place (mkdirSync at 1041, panel `--out` at 1047), so each repeat destroys the verdicts `pickLatestVerdicts`/`priorFindingsFor` would otherwise carry — the same "discarding their verdicts is not converging, it is forgetting" failure the `--fresh` refusal message names. Reported here because an added-but-bypassable gate reads as covered; the bound is a convergence policy rather than a permission gate, so this may sit better with the correctness lens.

samples.summary: The review base (and every missing intermediate) is created before any of the ownership/mode validation runs
samples.evidence: `mkdirSync(requested, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` at spec-to-pr.mjs:925 runs before the leaf check (939) and before the ancestor walk (959-966), so on a path whose ancestor turns out to be attacker-owned the command creates directories inside that attacker's tree and only then refuses. Impact is confined to leaving an empty 0700 directory behind — every write (`pr.diff`, `prior-findings.json`, `rebuttals.json`, the panel's `--out`) and the `--fresh` `rmSync` happen strictly after the refusal point, and the guard itself correctly rejects the squatted-ancestor and symlink-preplant cases I tried to walk. Noted only because validating the chain before creating anything under it would make the ordering self-evidently safe rather than safe-by-audit.

finding.summary: The round store is keyed on the branch NAME alone, so two checkouts with the same branch name share one carry-forward store — the exact cross-context prompt-injection channel `branchKey` was written to close for detached HEAD
finding.evidence:
`reviewBase(branch)` (spec-to-pr.mjs:771-775) derives the base from the branch string only: `path.join(os.tmpdir(), "wafflebase-self-review", `${safe}-${hash}`)`, where `hash = sha1(branch)`. Nothing in the key identifies the repository, worktree, or remote — `cmdReview` calls it as `reviewBase(branch)` at line 902 with `branch = branchKey(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD, …)`.

`branchKey`'s own docblock (lines 737-753) states the harm precisely for the detached-HEAD case: sharing a key means the checkouts "share a round counter … and, far worse, one carry-forward store — `priorFindingsFor` would read another change's verdicts and put their text into this round's verifier prompt." That harm is unaddressed for the much more common collision: two clones/worktrees on the same branch name.

Attack: a contributor controls both their branch NAME and its diff content. A maintainer who clones/worktrees the contributor's branch beside their own work — or simply has two checkouts on a common name such as `main`/`dev` — gets one shared base. `priorFindingsFor` (line 860-870) then reads `<base>/round-N/<lens>/verdict.json` written while reviewing the OTHER checkout and hands it to `prepareRoundInputs` → `panelArgs --prior-findings` (lines 1055-1062, 1086-1095), i.e. straight into the next round's verifier prompt. Lens verdict text is model output derived from the hostile diff, so a contributor who names their branch to collide can place chosen text in front of an agent session running in the maintainer's other checkout. The same collision also lets one checkout's rounds consume the other's three-round bound.

The per-user 0700 base limits this to a single user's checkouts, which is why this is `major` rather than `critical`. Fix: fold the repository identity (e.g. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, or the `origin` URL) into the hash alongside the branch.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `reviewBase` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:771-775) keys the round store solely on the branch string (`safe` slug + sha1 of the branch), with no repository/worktree/remote component, and `cmdReview` uses it as the default base at line 902 with `branch = branchKey(...)` from line 896. The carry-forward path off that shared base is live: `priorFindingsFor` (860-870) reads `<base>/round-N/<lens>/verdict.json`, `prepareRoundInputs` (1058, defined 675) writes the prior file, and `panelArgs` (1086-1095, defined 706) hands it to the panel as `--prior-findings`, so another checkout's model-produced verdict text reaches this round's verifier prompt. `carryForwardFindings` (scripts/agent/prior-findings.mjs:153) validates only shape/severity — nothing ties a carried finding to the repo or commit it came from. The surrounding hardening (0700 creation, `unsafeBaseReason` leaf+ancestor walk, `realpathSync`, lines 903-966) defends against a foreign user, not against two of the same user's checkouts colliding, so it is not an `already-guarded` case. The module's own branchKey docblock (736-753) names this exact harm for detached HEAD, confirming the cross-context prompt-injection framing is in the security lane; the shared base also lets one checkout's rounds consume the other's round bound (970-997). Same-user blast radius justifies major, not refutation.
